prompt: A basketball player makes $80\%$ of her free throws, independently. In a practice session she takes $25$ free throws. What is the expected number of makes?
hint: Each shot is an independent make or miss with the same chance, so the number of makes is a binomial variable. What is its mean?

hints.text: Each shot is an independent make or miss with the same chance, so the number of makes is a binomial variable. What is its mean?
The binomial mean is $np$. Here there are $n = 25$ shots with $p = 0.8$, so multiply $25 \times 0.8$.
$25 \times 0.8 = 20$, so she is expected to make $20$ free throws.

explanation: The number of makes $X$ counts successes in $25$ independent shots, so it is binomial with $n = 25$ and $p = 0.8$.
The mean of a binomial distribution is $\mu_X = np$, the number of trials times the chance of success.
$25 \times 0.8 = 20$, so the expected number of makes is $20$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Percent of the shots
steps: She makes $80\%$ of her shots in the long run.
Some sessions she makes more, some fewer, but 20 is the long-run average.
